title: El recibo está malo
desc: A bill that is wrong, and the man who cannot fix it
setting: The water bill says four times what you used. You are at the window with the paper in your hand.

steps.speaker: Empleado
steps.en: Good morning. How can I help you?

options.es: Buenos días. Fíjese que este recibo me llegó muy alto.
options.en: Good morning. The thing is, this bill came to me very high.
options.feedback: Fíjese warns him a problem is coming without making him the problem. That is how a counter complaint opens here.
Clear, and it puts the fault on the paper straight away. He will get defensive before you finish.
Ustedes makes him the company. Now he is defending it instead of helping you.

steps.speaker: Empleado
steps.es: A ver. ¿Cuánto pagó el mes pasado?
steps.en: Let us see. How much did you pay last month?

options.es: Trescientos. Aquí traigo el recibo anterior.
options.en: Three hundred. I have the previous bill here.
options.feedback: A number and the proof. That is the whole argument won in one sentence.
Close enough to be believed, weak enough to be argued with. Bring the paper next time.
Now there is nothing to compare it with and no case to make.

steps.speaker: Empleado
steps.es: Ah, sí. Aquí hay un error. Pero yo no lo puedo cambiar.
steps.en: Ah, yes. There is a mistake here. But I cannot change it.

options.es: Entiendo. ¿Y con quién tengo que hablar?
options.en: I understand. And who do I have to talk to?
options.feedback: You took the no and asked for the next door. He will open it for you now.

options.en: And so what do I do?
options.feedback: Fair, and it hands him a problem instead of a question he can answer.

options.es: Entonces para qué está usted ahí.
options.en: Then what are you sitting there for.
options.feedback: One sentence and you have lost the only person in the building who was on your side.

steps.speaker: Empleado
steps.es: Tiene que ir a la oficina central. Lleve los dos recibos.
steps.en: You have to go to the head office. Take both bills.

options.es: Va pues. Muchas gracias por la ayuda.
options.en: Right then. Thank you very much for the help.
options.feedback: He did help, and thanking him is what makes the next window easier.
It accepts. He went and found the error for you and got nothing for it.
True, and he heard it. That trip was going to happen either way.
